title: 2026-03-30-quality-observability-compare-lab-demo-aurora-ventures

API perf profile: latency and cost tradeoffs

summary: Redwood AE/SE ran an end-to-end demo of the quality observability features focused on prompt sets, regression alerts, and A/B comparisons. Customer is evaluating hosted vs private deployment for regulated portfolio summaries, wants pilot metrics, security artifacts, and a suggested traffic split strategy. Action items: send security pack, pilot pricing, and a short benchmark plan.
action_items: Maya Patel - Share SOC2 summary, VPC deployment blueprint, and KMS integration notes by 2026-04-02
Ethan Brooks - Prepare a 3-run latency/cost benchmark plan (short & long context) by 2026-04-05
Liam Chen - Provide 3 representative prompt sets and expected success criteria by 2026-04-07

Send SOW for 2-week evaluation pilot and pricing tiers
Share console recording and quickstart notebook link
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-03-30 15:00 UTC, Duration ~48m, Recording started
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Liam (CTO Aurora), Sara (ML Engineer), Priya (Security), Noah (PM)

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. quick round robin — can you confirm roles?
[00:07] Liam: Yeah I'm Liam, CTO at Aurora, we run summarization pipelines for investor updates, and we are evaluating vendor inference for compliance and cost.
[00:12] Sara: Sara here, ML eng, owns prompt sets and evaluation pipelines.
[00:16] Priya: Priya, security and infra. focused on VPC and key management needs.
[00:20] Noah: Noah, product — mostly success criteria and timeline.
[00:24] Maya: Great — quick agenda: console walkthrough for quality observability, demo prompt sets/regression alerts, then A/B compare and API perf. Ethan will lead the live demo. any must-see items?
[00:33] Liam: Security artifacts up front would be helpful — SOC 2 and where logs live.
[00:37] Priya: Also want to understand audit logs for prompts and outputs, retention options.
[00:41] Maya: We'll cover that and follow up with docs.

[02:05] Ethan: Jumping in — opening Redwood Console -> Quality -> Prompt Sets. so here you can create a prompt set, attach labels and expected outputs, and map them to an eval suite. You can see we imported a set earlier: investor-summaries-v1. note: transcription sometimes shows 'investor summers' in autosave — that's the speech-to-text quirk.
[02:28] Sara: when you say labels, are they freeform or schema-driven?
[02:34] Ethan: Both — you can define a JSON schema expected field or free text labels. schema-driven helps with automated regression metrics.
[03:05] Ethan: Now the regression alerts tab — you can set baseline window, sensitivity, and choose metrics: ROUGE, factuality score, hallucination heuristics, and custom regex checks. here's an example alert: stability drop >5% over 3 runs triggers Slack and PagerDuty.
[03:29] Priya: Does the alert payload include raw output? Need to be careful with PII.
[03:33] Ethan: Good call. By default alerts include metric summaries and example ids, not full rawtext. You can toggle redaction and opt for pointers to encrypted blob storage behind your VPC.
[03:47] Liam: How does this work across model variants? we test gptish-7b-quant and a larger hosted model.
[03:54] Ethan: You can route comparisons to any model in the catalog, and the A/B compare binds traffic splits and stores paired outputs for side-by-side metrics. KV cache differences may affect tokens billed so we show token delta in the compare.

[05:10] [Audio glitch for ~3s — transcript imperfect]
[05:14] Ethan: Back — console demo continuing: traffic split UI — you pick a primary (prod) and a challenger, set percent, and choose evaluation windows. We also surface rollback recommendations if challenger causes latency regressions or quality drops.
[05:33] Noah: what's the minimum sample size for statistically meaningful drift?
[05:37] Ethan: Depends on variance — we surface a recommended sample size based on observed metric variance. for summary tasks with high variance we suggest 2k responses for a robust t-test, but you can run bootstrap for smaller samples.

[07:02] Sara: Can I upload my own metrics? we run custom entailment and fact-checker.
[07:07] Ethan: Yes — there's an API and SDK to ingest external metrics per example id; the console will join them and include them in the alerting pipeline.
[07:15] Maya: Quick note on labels and prompt sets — good to version both. we keep prompt set version tied to rollout so you can rollback to a prior prompt slice.

[09:00] Ethan: Now switching to the API demo — hitting the Redwood inference endpoint with a prompt set runner. i'll run three prompts from the investor-summaries set with both models.
[09:18] [45s] Ethan: Running — response times: challenger avg 320ms p50, primary avg 140ms p50. token costs displayed per-call. you'll see these in the telemetry panel.
[09:46] Sara: big delta — the challenger is much slower. is that model on dedicated or hosted?
[09:50] Ethan: Challenger is a larger hosted instance; there are autoscaling tradeoffs. we recommend dedicated pools for stable p50 under tight latency SLOs.

[11:12] Priya: about data residency — if we do private deployment, do logs stay in our VPC?
[11:18] Ethan: Yes — with Private mode, the control plane can be customer-managed and logs can be pushed to your logging endpoint or S3 behind your KMS. we'll share the network diagram.

[12:30] Ethan: Back to console -> A/B compare results page. shows paired outputs, diff highlights, automatic score deltas. here's an example where challenger increased verboseness but dropped factuality. you can filter by label and by user cohort.
[12:55] Liam: Can we run cohort splits by portfolio type?
[12:58] Ethan: Yes — cohorts are first-class. you can tag requests with metadata fields (portfolio_id, region) and run splits and metrics per cohort.

[14:20] [small crosstalk]
[14:24] Ethan: I'm going to show regression alert rule authoring — create rule => metric OR composite, choose window, set mute periods. there's also a canary policy: run 5% initial traffic for 24h before expanding.
[14:45] Noah: For pilot, we want to do 10% traffic for two weeks. can we do progressive ramp with manual approvals?
[14:50] Ethan: Yes. we'll show automated gates and require manual approvals in the rollout policy.

[16:05] Sara: curious about storing raw outputs — cost and retention policy?
[16:09] Ethan: By default we store a short retention (30 days) in encrypted storage. You can increase retention or export to your S3. we show token-level cost breakdown to help estimate storage costs.

[18:40] Maya: Let's surface some of the tricky bits customers ask — latency vs cost. often they ask: do we pick quantized smaller models or use caching?
[18:48] Ethan: caching helps for prefix-heavy workloads. our KV cache and prefix caching can reduce per-token compute — we calculate effective cost per generated token across traffic patterns. quantization reduces memory and can improve throughput but might alter output quality — so run A/B compare and monitor quality metrics.

[20:12] [background noise for a few seconds — transcript fuzzy]
[20:20] Priya: security quick question: SSO and RBAC, can we link to our IdP and restrict access to prompt sets?
[20:25] Maya: Yes, SAML/SSO supported, SCIM provisioning, and RBAC at namespace and prompt-set level. audit logs show who ran what eval and when.

[22:02] Ethan: Now a quick deep-dive: metric derivation. we compute n-gram and embedding-based similarity, plus custom model-based hallucination score if you upload a fact-checker model. sample scoring code is in the SDK.
[22:19] Sara: do you support human-in-the-loop labeling for ambiguous cases?
[22:22] Ethan: Yes — you can route samples to a review queue, annotate, and push labels back to the dataset. integrates with our built-in annotator or third-party tools via webhooks.

[25:00] Maya: Example of an alert firing — here's a synthetic demo: baseline factuality 92% drops to 85% after a model swap. alert fires, we show paired diffs and a recommended rollback.
[25:16] Liam: will that create noise? we have lots of small fluctuations.
[25:20] Ethan: you can tune sensitivity and add suppressions for transient traffic anomalies. also use composite metrics to require multiple signals.

[26:45] Noah: what about integration with our CI? we want to gate model rollouts via PRs and automated tests.
[26:52] Ethan: there's an API endpoint to trigger an eval run from your CI; you can block merges if metrics don't meet thresholds. we can provide a GitHub action example.

[29:10] [five seconds pause]
[29:16] Priya: for private/on-prem, what's the ops responsibility split?
[29:21] Ethan: With Private, Redwood provides the control plane but it runs in your VPC; you control the compute, network, and keys. we offer an on-call runbook for initial setup and a managed option where we handle infra under a support contract.

[31:00] Sara: can we compare prompt variants systematically? we have 12 prompt permutations.
[31:05] Ethan: yes — you can upload them as a prompt set with a variant id, run an A/B matrix, and the console shows pairwise comparisons, performance heatmap, and best-worst ranking.

[33:40] Ethan: showing the API logs and traces — each call has a trace id, model variant, token counts, and a link to the paired output in the compare UI. you can also export traces to your observability stack.

[35:10] Liam: on pricing — want a pilot with predictable spend. can you send a tailored SOW?
[35:16] Maya: absolutely. we propose a 2-week pilot with dedicated capacity for stability, include cost estimates, and success criteria.

[36:40] [short laughter]
[36:44] Noah: timeline — if we like the pilot, target production in Q2?
[36:50] Maya: Pilot in April, production target end of May is feasible.

[38:10] Ethan: demo wrap-up: key takeaways: console supports prompt-set versioning, automated regression alerts with redaction options, A/B compare with paired outputs and token delta, cohort splits, and private deployment options for logs/KMS.

[39:02] Priya: we'll need the full security pack — network diagrams, SOC2, iso docs, and a data flow for audit.
[39:10] Maya: I'll send that and link to the VPC design doc.

[40:00] Sara: quick ask — can you run a short benchmark with our 5 sample prompts to show p50/p95 and token cost?
[40:07] Ethan: yes — I'll draft a 3-run plan and include short & long context runs.

[41:32] Maya: Recap of next steps: we'll send security docs, pilot SOW, a short benchmark plan, and schedule pilot kickoff. any blockers?
[41:45] Liam: none immediate, just internal signoff.
[41:48] Noah: I'll coordinate calendar invites.

[43:00] [final clarifying Q&A, minor crosstalk]
[47:30] Maya: thanks everyone; we'll follow up with the packet. meeting ends.
questions: Can alerts include raw outputs or only pointers?
How are cohorts defined and used for A/B splits?
What's the recommended sample size for statistically meaningful comparisons?
